name: ADS1299-4PAGR
title: 4-, 6- and 8-channel 24-bit delta-sigma ADC with PGA for EEG and biopotential measurement
summary: ADS1299-4, ADS1299-6 and ADS1299 are biopotential front ends with four, six or eight channels, each a low-noise PGA (gain 1 to 24) feeding its own 24-bit delta-sigma converter, all sampling at once at 250 SPS to 16 kSPS. On the die sit a 4.5 V reference, a 2.048 MHz oscillator, a per-channel input multiplexer with test, temperature and supply signals, lead-off detection and a bias-drive amplifier for the patient. The host talks over SPI; several devices can share a bus or be daisy-chained. TQFP-64, -40 °C to +85 °C.

circuits.title: External reference driver
circuits.description: A REF5025 runs from 5 V; its output has 10 µF to ground and passes 100 Ω into 100 µF, a band-limiting filter ahead of the OPA350 buffer's noninverting input. The buffer drives the VREFP pin through 10 Ω, with 10 µF and 0.1 µF from the pin to ground; 100 kΩ feeds back from the pin side of the 10 Ω to the inverting input, and 22 nF connects the buffer output to its inverting input. The OPA350 runs from +5 V with 0.1 µF. The REF5025 TRIM pin has 1 µF to ground. The internal reference buffer is powered down (PD_REFBUF = 0) when this circuit drives VREFP.
notes: The REF5025 ground pin is not shown in the circuit.

circuits.title: Single-supply operation (5 V and 3.3 V)
circuits.description: One 5 V analog supply and one 3.3 V digital supply, with AVSS and DGND both on ground. AVDD and AVDD1 share the 5 V rail with 1 µF and 0.1 µF; DVDD has 0.1 µF and 1 µF. VREFN is grounded, with 0.1 µF and 10 µF from VREFP to it. VCAP4 has 1 µF, VCAP3 has 1 µF in parallel with 0.1 µF, VCAP2 has 1 µF and VCAP1 has 100 µF, all to ground. RESV1 is grounded. Supply, reference and VCAP capacitors all sit right at the package.

circuits.title: Bipolar supply operation (±2.5 V and 3.3 V)
circuits.description: The analog side runs from ±2.5 V: AVDD and AVDD1 on +2.5 V with 1 µF and 0.1 µF to ground, AVSS and AVSS1 on -2.5 V with 1 µF and 0.1 µF to ground. DVDD is 3.3 V against DGND with 0.1 µF and 1 µF. VREFN sits on the -2.5 V rail, with 0.1 µF and 10 µF from VREFP to it; the VCAP capacitors (1 µF on VCAP4, 1 µF plus 0.1 µF on VCAP3, 1 µF on VCAP2, 100 µF on VCAP1) return to the -2.5 V rail too. RESV1 goes to digital ground. All of these capacitors sit right at the package.

circuits.title: EEG acquisition, sequential montage
circuits.description: Each channel reads the voltage between two neighbouring electrodes: electrodes 1 and 2 go to IN1P and IN1N, 3 and 4 to IN2P and IN2N, and so on for the other channels. Every electrode passes through its own RFilt, and one CFilt across each channel's two inputs makes a differential low-pass whose rejection of common-mode does not hang on part matching. Inside, each PGA output feeds the bias amplifier's inverting input through 220 kΩ when its BIASPn or BIASNn bit is set; the amplifier, referenced to (AVDD + AVSS) / 2 with BIASREF_INT set, drives the bias electrode through RP, with RF and CF from BIASOUT back to BIASINV setting its gain and bandwidth. The analog side runs from ±2.5 V.
notes: RFilt, CFilt, RF, CF and RP carry no values; RFilt has a lower limit set by medical safety standards and CFilt is chosen for the cutoff.

circuits.title: EEG acquisition, referential montage
circuits.description: Every electrode is read against one reference electrode. Electrodes 1 to 4 (and on, for the other channels) go through RFilt to IN1P to IN4P; the reference electrode goes through its own RFilt to SRB1, and setting the SRB1 bit in MISC1 switches SRB1 onto all the inverting inputs. A CFilt from each noninverting input to SRB1 completes each channel's differential filter. The bias loop is the same as in the sequential montage: each PGA output into BIASINV through 220 kΩ when selected, RF and CF around the amplifier, RP to the bias electrode, reference (AVDD + AVSS) / 2 inside. Supplies are ±2.5 V.

circuits.title: 10 Hz small-signal test setup
circuits.description: A 33 µVRMS, 10 Hz generator is cut down by a 952 kΩ over 10.3 kΩ divider, then passes 4.99 kΩ into a 4.7 nF capacitor across the channel inputs; the noninverting input gets the signal and the inverting input sits on the generator ground. About 3.5 µVRMS at 10 Hz reaches the inputs. The device runs from ±2.5 V. Any channel can be used.

operation.text: ADS1299-4, ADS1299-6 and ADS1299 differ only in channel count (4, 6, 8) and share pinout, registers and package. Channels 5 to 8 exist on the ADS1299 only, 5 and 6 also on the ADS1299-6. The family is pin compatible with the ADS129x. The ID register's NU_CH bits tell the three apart.

Lowering the data rate averages more and lowers noise; raising the PGA gain lowers input-referred noise. The noise tables are typical values at 25 °C with a 5 V analog supply, inputs shorted, averaged over several devices; at the lower data rates peak-to-peak is about 6.6 times RMS. They hold for the internal reference and also for a low-noise external one such as the REF5045.

Each channel has its own multiplexer, PGA and second-order delta-sigma modulator with a sinc3 decimation filter; all channels convert at the same moment and the same rate. Shared blocks: 4.5 V reference, 2.048 MHz oscillator, bias amplifier, lead-off excitation and comparators, test signal, temperature sensor, four GPIO pins and the SPI port. The EEG-specific circuits can be turned off so the part works as a general multichannel data converter.

Per channel, CHnSET MUXn picks the electrode inputs, a short to (VREFP + VREFN) / 2 for offset and noise checks, the test signal, the temperature sensor, a supply monitor, or a bias measurement; BIAS_MEAS in CONFIG3 and SRB1 in MISC1 add more routes. SRB1, SRB2 and BIASIN serve every channel alike. Lead-off excitation and the lead-off comparators connect ahead of the multiplexer switches.

MUXn = 101 puts the internal test signal on the channel so the signal chain can be checked at start-up. CONFIG2 sets it: amplitude 1 × or 2 × (VREFP – VREFN) / 2400, pulsed at fCLK / 2^21 or fCLK / 2^20, or dc.

Two diodes run at current densities 16 to 1 give a voltage proportional to absolute temperature, read with MUXn = 100. The package couples tightly to the board, so the reading follows board temperature, a little high because of the part's own heating. Convert the code to microvolts first, then use the temperature equation.
MUXn = 011 measures supplies: on channels 1, 2, 5, 6, 7 and 8 the input is 0.5 × (AVDD + AVSS); on channels 3 and 4 it is DVDD / 4. Use gain 1 so the PGA does not saturate.

BIASIN mainly brings the bias signal back to an electrode if the bias electrode comes off, but it can also be read as a single-ended input against BIASREF on any channel by setting MUXn = 010 and BIAS_MEAS = 1.

Inputs are fully differential and go straight to the PGA; the differential range is ±VREF / gain. Driven pseudo-differentially, INxN holds a fixed level (mid-supply is best) and INxP swings around it, so the common-mode moves with the signal and must stay in range at both extremes. Driven fully differentially, the two inputs swing in opposite phase by ±½ VREF / gain about a fixed common-mode, which gives the full dynamic range; set that common-mode at (AVDD + AVSS) / 2.

The PGA is differential in and out with gains 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12 and 24 (CHnSET). Its CMOS inputs have negligible current noise. At gain 12 its gain string totals 39.6 kΩ (two 18.15 kΩ and one 3.3 kΩ), which draws current from the inputs' amplifiers whenever a differential signal is present, on top of the quiescent current.

The PGA amplifier outputs cannot come within 200 mV of AVDD or AVSS without saturating, so the input common-mode is limited by supply, gain and the largest differential signal, as in the common-mode range equation.

The second-order modulator samples at fMOD = fCLK / 2 and shapes its noise up to fMOD / 2; the decimation filter removes it and also serves as the antialias filter, so only a simple analog filter is needed in front.

The 4.5 V reference is made against AVSS from a bandgap through a divider (9.8 kΩ, 13.4 kΩ and 36.85 kΩ for 4.5 V) and needs 100 µF on VCAP1 and 10 µF on VREFP; tie VREFN to AVSS when using it. The external capacitors set how much reference noise gets through: for high-end EEG choose them for a bandwidth under 10 Hz. Start-up time is 150 ms.

With PD_REFBUF = 0 the internal buffer is off and VREFP can be driven from outside; two cascaded devices can share one internal reference the same way. The part powers up with the buffer off, in external reference mode. The external reference input looks like 5.6 kΩ.

Each channel has a sinc3 filter whose decimation ratio, set by DR in CONFIG1 for all channels at once, trades resolution for rate. Its notches fall at the data rate and its multiples. After an input step it needs 3 × tDR to settle; the passband repeats around every multiple of fMOD, so the input RC filter must attenuate interference near those frequencies. Higher data rates are used in EEG for ac lead-off detection.

CLKSEL high selects the internal oscillator, low the CLK pin; with the oscillator in use, CLK_EN puts its clock out on CLK for other devices, otherwise CLK is high impedance. The oscillator is trimmed at room temperature (±0.5 %) and holds ±2.5 % over temperature; it suits battery systems. Stop an external clock during power-down to save power.

Four GPIO pins, each an input or output by GPIOC; GPIOD reads the pin level in either direction and sets it when an output. After power-on or reset they are inputs and must not float; tie unused ones to DGND.

Once some channels feed the bias derivation and the feedback parts are fitted round the amplifier, the bias signal appears on BIASOUT. It can be fed to BIASIN, filtered or directly, and from there onto any electrode by MUXn = 110 (positive side) or 111 (negative side), so the electrode that drives the body can be changed on the fly. BIASIN can also be routed to an unused channel (MUXn = 010 with BIAS_MEAS = 1) and measured against BIASREF, which is (AVDD + AVSS) / 2 when internal; useful while debugging.

An excitation current is injected and the resulting voltage shows whether an electrode is off. LOFF_SENSP and LOFF_SENSN pick which inputs are checked; excitation can be turned off leaving only the sensing. Two methods differ in the excitation frequency.

Excitation is dc: outside 10 MΩ pull-up and pull-down resistors, or the internal current source and sink (ILEAD_OFF sets 6 nA, 24 nA, 6 µA or 24 µA; LOFF_FLIP swaps which side goes up). One input is pulled toward the supply, the other toward ground, so an open electrode saturates the channel; the output code shows that one side is off, and the comparators, with thresholds set by COMP_TH, show which. Their results are in LOFF_STATP and LOFF_STATN, which also ride in the data stream. The current source loads the input less than 10 MΩ resistors. PD_LOFF_COMP turns the comparators off when not needed.

The current source and sink alternate at 7.8 Hz or 31.2 Hz (FLEAD_OFF), inside the signal band; the channel converts the response like any signal, and its amplitude at the excitation frequency yields the electrode impedance. For continuous out-of-band checking, an outside ac current has to be applied to the inputs and processed digitally.

At power-up, with the bias amplifier off, a current source and comparator check whether the bias electrode is connected, the comparator level setting the impedance limit; BIAS_STAT reports it. With the amplifier on, the current source does nothing and only the comparator watches the amplifier output, using the same LOFF[7:5] thresholds as the negative inputs.

The bias amplifier senses the common-mode of the selected electrodes (BIAS_SENSP, BIAS_SENSN; each PGA output joins through 220 kΩ) and drives the body with the inverted common-mode, holding the common-mode in a narrow range against mains and lighting interference. All its pins come out, so the loop parts are the user's choice and loop stability depends on the system. Typical feedback is 1 MΩ with 1.5 nF. Its reference is (AVDD + AVSS) / 2 inside or a divider on BIASREF (BIASREF_INT). PD_BIAS turns it off when unused.
When devices share a bias drive, only one bias amplifier stays powered; the others are powered down with PD_BIAS and their bias-derivation outputs join the active one's inverting input.

START high for at least 2 tCLK, or the START command, begins conversions; with START low and no command, there is no DRDY. Hold the pin low when running by command. SINGLE_SHOT in CONFIG4 picks continuous or single-shot. In systems with several devices, START lines them up.

After START goes high, DRDY goes high and its next fall marks the first fully settled result, tSETTLE later (settling-time table, in tCLK, depending on DR). Then DRDY falls every tDR. When unread data are replaced in the output register, DRDY first rises for 4 tCLK. With START held high, an input step takes 3 × tDR, and the fourth DRDY brings settled data.

Pull RESET low for its minimum width, or send RESET (effective at falling SCLK edge 8). Initialization takes 18 tCLK, returning registers to defaults and starting the conversion cycle. Any WREG that changes CONFIG1 also resets the digital filter.
PWDN low turns off everything on the chip; when it returns high, the oscillator and reference need time to wake.

DRDY falls when new data is ready, whatever CS does. The first falling SCLK edge sets it high again, whether data is being read or a command sent. Reading with RDATA may run past the next DRDY without corrupting data.

Data can be read continuously (RDATAC) or on command (RDATA). The MSB appears with the first rising SCLK edge; keep DIN low while reading. A frame is 24 status bits then 24 bits per channel (216 bits for the ADS1299): status is 1100, LOFF_STATP, LOFF_STATN and GPIO bits 4 to 7. Channel data are twos complement, MSB first; a powered-down channel reads 0 but keeps its slot. With DAISY_EN = 1, extra SCLKs in RDATAC repeat the frame from the first byte (multiple readback).

Conversions run from START high or the START command until START goes low or STOP is sent, the conversion under way being finished. Meet tSDSU or tDSHD (16 tCLK) relative to DRDY to stop before or after the next result. START can be tied high to run all the time. Going from single-shot to continuous, toggle START or send STOP then START.

With SINGLE_SHOT = 1, each START high or START command gives one conversion; DRDY falls and stays low, read or not. Toggle START or send START again for the next. Each start resets the filter, so the effective rate drops by four, aliasing is more of a risk and the host does more work. It suits uneven or non-standard rates.
24-bit twos complement; one code is (2 × VREF / gain) / 2^24. Positive full scale reads 7FFFFFh, negative full scale 800000h, and larger inputs stay at these codes.

CS low enables the SPI and has to remain low through the whole transaction; CS high puts DOUT in high impedance and resets the serial interface, while conversions and DRDY carry on (SCLK still forces DRDY high). Wait at least 4 tCLK after the last clock before raising CS.

SCLK has Schmitt-trigger hysteresis, yet glitches can still shift data, so keep it clean. DIN is taken on the falling edge and DOUT changes on the rising edge. Always send the full set of clocks for a command, or the interface can lock up until CS is taken high. The slowest usable SCLK depends on channel count, resolution and data rate: 110 kHz for the 8-channel ADS1299 at 500 SPS.
The device reads commands while it shifts data out, so whatever is on DIN during a read must be valid; send NOP (zeros) when there is no command.

System commands and RDATA are decoded at falling SCLK edge 7, register commands at edge 8. Each byte takes 4 tCLK to decode (tSDECODE, 1.96 µs at 2.048 MHz), so bytes of a multi-byte command must be at least 4 tCLK apart: at 16 MHz SCLK a byte takes 500 ns and needs added delay; at 4 MHz a byte takes 2 µs and bytes can be sent back to back.
STANDBY shuts everything except the reference; send only WAKEUP afterwards. WAKEUP leaves standby; the next command needs a 4 tCLK delay. Both may be sent at any SCLK rate and at any time.

START starts conversions (no effect if already running); STOP lets the current conversion finish and halts. Hold the START pin low when using them, and leave 4 tCLK between a START and a STOP sent right after it. RESET returns registers to defaults and restarts the filter cycle in 18 tCLK; send nothing meanwhile.

RDATAC, the power-up default, puts each result in the output register at every DRDY, ready to be clocked out; while in it, send SDATAC before any other command (SDATAC needs 4 tCLK before the next command). Do not issue RDATAC within 4 tCLK of a DRDY pulse (tUPDATE). RDATA, used outside RDATAC, loads the latest result after DRDY falls, with no wait afterwards. For either, START must be high or the START command sent. RDATAC suits loggers whose registers are set once; RDATA suits systems that change registers between conversions.

Two command bytes, 001r rrrr or 010r rrrr (start address) and 000n nnnn (count less one), then the data, MSB first. In RREG the first register's MSB appears on the 17th SCLK rising edge; RREG needs SDATAC first when in RDATAC mode. Keep CS low throughout and meet tSDECODE between bytes.

Unused analog inputs: channel powered down, pins tied to AVDD. If the bias amplifier is unused, power it down and leave BIASOUT and BIASINV open; BIASIN can float or go to AVSS. BIASREF, SRB1 and SRB2 go to AVSS or float. Unused digital inputs must not float, which could raise supply leakage; mode pins go to DVDD or DGND through 10 kΩ or more. Pull DRDY up weakly if unused and tie DAISY_IN to DGND when not chaining.

Power up as in the power-up sequencing; either supply a 2.048 MHz clock with CLKSEL = 0 or set CLKSEL = 1 and let the oscillator start. Set PWDN and RESET high, wait tPOR (and until VCAP1 ≥ 1.1 V), pulse RESET and wait 18 tCLK. Send SDATAC (the part wakes in RDATAC). For the internal reference write CONFIG3 = E0h and let it settle. Write CONFIG1 = 96h (fMOD / 4096), CONFIG2 = C0h and every CHnSET = 01h (inputs shorted), set START = 1 (DRDY then runs at fCLK / 8192), send RDATAC and check the noise, reading 24 + n × 24 bits at each DRDY. Then SDATAC, CONFIG2 = D0h and CHnSET = 05h for a square-wave test signal of 1 mV × VREF / 2.4 on every channel, RDATAC, and read again.
DC lead-off on all channels: LOFF = 0x13 (thresholds 95 % and 5 %), CONFIG4 = 0x02 (comparators on), LOFF_SENSP = 0xFF and LOFF_SENSN = 0xFF.

Bias from the average of channels 1 to 3: BIAS_SENSP = 0x07, BIAS_SENSN = 0x07, CONFIG3 = x1xx 1100b (amplifier on, internal BIASREF). To route BIASOUT, wired outside to BIASIN, onto channel 4's negative side and measure it on channel 5: CONFIG3 = xxx1 1100b, CH4SET = xxxx 0111b, CH5SET = xxxx 0010b.

Noise coupled onto the body moves the electrodes' common-mode, which the PGA headroom limits. Where a drive electrode is fitted, the bias amplifier holds the body at mid-supply or the BIASREF voltage; using the measuring electrodes as its feedback inputs (BIAS_SENSP, BIAS_SENSN) holds it more firmly. A three-electrode example uses 1 MΩ and 1.5 nF between BIASOUT and BIASINV, with protection and antialiasing blocks in each electrode lead.

With one CS per device, n devices need 3 + n signals. To use one internal oscillator, set one device's CLKSEL = 1 and CLK_EN = 1 and feed its CLK to the others. START synchronizes the devices, the START-to-DRDY delay being fixed for a data rate. Devices connect either in cascade or in a daisy chain.
All devices share DOUT, SCLK and DIN, and every device gets a separate CS; a deselected device leaves DOUT in high impedance. Two 8-channel devices make 16 channels. This suits most systems.

Set DAISY_EN = 0 in CONFIG1 to select daisy-chain mode. All devices share SCLK, DIN and CS; the second device's DOUT goes to the first device's DAISY_IN, and device 1's status and data come out first, then device 2's. Multiple readback is not available. An ADS1299 chains with another ADS1299, an ADS1299-6 or an ADS1299-4. If all devices take the same settings, DIN can be shared too and the SPI needs four signals however many devices, but then no bias driver sharing is possible and an outside clock is needed. Data shift out on the rising edge and into DAISY_IN on the falling edge, which allows a fast SCLK but makes the link sensitive to board delays: a star SCLK, short DOUT runs, buffers or a D flip-flop clocked on inverted SCLK between DOUT and DAISY_IN help. Data spread across byte boundaries have to be reassembled in software.

The ADS1299 connects to the electrodes with no added gain or buffer stage; at some rates and gains its noise is well under 1 µVRMS, against a smallest EEG signal of 10 µV peak. Its 24 bits let the signal be dc coupled with its offset, where older systems high-pass filtered and used 12- to 16-bit converters. Low input bias current keeps cable leakage tiny; dc input impedance is 1 GΩ min with lead-off off, 500 MΩ typ with the lead-off current on.

RFilt and CFilt form the low-pass; use one differential CFilt across the inputs rather than capacitors to ground, which improves CMRR by removing dependence on matching. The corner can sit well above the data rate, but must stop aliasing around fMOD (1.024 MHz with a 2.048 MHz clock). Medical standards put a lower limit on RFilt. Against high-frequency EMI, small common-mode capacitors to ground can be added, 10 to 20 times smaller than the differential one so CMRR suffers little.

The bias amplifier both keeps the electrodes' common-mode inside the rails, which makes dc coupling possible, and feeds back inverted common-mode to cancel mains interference. Turn it on with PD_BIAS, take the internal mid-supply with BIASREF_INT and pick electrodes with BIAS_SENSP and BIAS_SENSN. It passes common-mode only; its dc gain is set by the feedback resistor and the number of inputs selected, and Cf sets its bandwidth, which must cover the common-mode signals to be cancelled.
With 3.5 µVRMS at 10 Hz on the inputs, the offset-calibrated output shows the sine clearly; the single-ended, unshielded setup picked up mains, removed with a digital low-pass filter.

Three supplies: AVDD, AVDD1 and DVDD, unipolar or bipolar. Keep AVDD and AVDD1 quiet; AVDD1 feeds the charge pump and carries transients at fCLK, so give AVDD1 and AVSS1 their own star connections back to AVDD and AVSS. Remove supply noise that is not synchronous with the part. Bypass each supply with 10 µF and 0.1 µF ceramics. Keep digital return currents away from the analog return path.

Use small multilayer ceramics. On boards subject to vibration, VCAP1 should be a non-ferroelectric type (tantalum or C0G/NPO): X7R, X5R, X8R and other class 2 and 3 dielectrics are piezoelectric and turn vibration into noise, and with the internal reference noise on VCAP1 degrades performance.

Hold every digital and analog input low until the supplies are steady. Then start the clock on CLK, wait tPOR (2^18 tCLK), and reset by pin or command once tPOR has passed or VCAP1 exceeds 1.1 V, whichever is later; VCAP1 charges at the rate set by its capacitor. Program the registers after RESET is released.

Keep analog parts and digital parts (microcontrollers, FPGAs, radios, switching regulators) in separate areas and keep digital traces clear of analog traces. A split ground is optional; if used, join the halves at the ADC. Fill unused signal-layer area with ground and keep return paths unbroken under signals. Bypass capacitors go next to the part on its own layer, with no vias between them and the pins. Put a high-quality capacitor, C0G (NPO) best, across each differential input. A two-layer board works, with analog inputs on the left, digital on the right and power pours above and below the part.
